summary: Plausible, self-gated, shape-scoped change to kernel P at NF=2/4 only (T 9..32). The NF=1 shapes and T>32 shapes act as in-run controls. Run it now on master as a plain check with no companions, and judge it on the dl_pooler_router P rows and the prepare P-timing line, not the headline (+0.3-0.5% at most).
justification: The data support the target. The prepare timing (job 81ee6714) gives P at 20.7 us at T=1, 21.9 at T=8 and 26.4 at T=32 (2.85 TB/s), and the profiles show P<2> at 25.1 us (sliding decode_16) and P<4> at 27.0/26.6 us (decode_32), against ~15.7 us for 75.5 MB at the 4.8 TB/s floor. So 4-5 us is recoverable, and REWRITE_READ lists this exact change as stage item 3. The geometry checks out on master's source: K=8192 is 128 blocks of 64, split 21x5+23=128; 4608 rows give 36 wide tiles, so 216 CTAs as today; smem is 4x(16 KB + NF KB) = 72/80 KB, 2 CTAs/SM fits; launch_bounds(256,2) allows 128 regs, and the NF=4 accumulator is only ~16 regs/lane. The expected directions fit the weights: decode_32 sliding -5/247 is about 2%, full decode_32 and full decode_16 are under 1% and will read as flat, and decode_1/verify are controls. WEAKEST LINK: the diagnosis. 'x re-read from L2' is asserted, not shown. x adds ~37.7 MB of L2 traffic over 26 us (~1.4 TB/s), well below H200 L2 bandwidth. Master's NF=2/4 already runs at 2 CTAs/SM (occupancy [3,2,2]), and the 216-CTA grid places at most ~2 CTAs per SM at every NF. So the T-dependence more likely comes from per-stage consumer time: x ldmatrix plus NF times the mma per W fragment, with only 8 warps per SM to hide it. The wide variant also changes that, since it doubles the warps per SM (8 -> 16) and halves the K per stage. A gain is therefore a real gain of the variant, but it does not prove the L2 re-read story. The residual risk is a wash: 4 stages of 64-K hold half the K-depth in flight per CTA of today's 4 x 128-K. Bytes in flight per CTA stay the same (16 KB/stage), but a 128-row CTA now needs the same ring to cover twice the rows.
confounders: small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl: P is this hypothesis's own kernel, so this is the base, not a confounder. Its PDL pre-wait prefetch of stages 0-2 is kept. On master the predecessor is SGLang's attn_boundary, which never triggers launch_dependents (REWRITE_READ: PDL bought 0.3 us). The P row is therefore not inflated by griddepcontrol.wait time, and the measurement on master is clean.
stack-align-par-sidestream-sliding1: it touches T>32 dispatch and sliding batch-1 attention only. It does not touch P at T 9..32, so it is not a confounder.

The other landed items (marlin-block-m-cap-16, fa3 pairing, router-hilo parity, post-expert-norm) do not touch kernel P's launch or traffic. One indirect path: P's split-K sum order changes (SPLIT 6 vs 3), so logits differ in the last bits and could flip near-tie routing into Marlin. That is tolerance-only, and Marlin's +-20-40 us profile noise dwarfs any timing effect, so the Marlin rows must not be read as part of this result.
interference: No companion is needed. A gain shows on the P<2>/P<4> rows of decode_16/32. A loss is explained by the logged occupancy and fallback lines (occupancy < 2 sends the change back to the current kernel per NF). The only within-change ambiguity is mechanism attribution (x re-read vs warps per SM vs K-depth per stage). That does not affect the land/no-land decision, so a control is not worth a check. INTERACTION WITH THE RUNNING CHECKS (dl-route-warp-topk-pdl b471a950, boundaries-unpooler-pdl-small-t 1dfe83fd, and dense-chain-stage2-attn-side-pdl b31b8453), which all edit the same _DL_CUDA TU: (1) dl-route-warp-topk-pdl inserts griddepcontrol.launch_dependents into dl_pooler_router_kernel after the K loop and PDL-launches R. If it lands first, the wide variant must get the same griddep_launch() after its K loop, or the R overlap is lost at T 9..32 and the restack reads as a loss on R, not P. (2) boundaries-unpooler-pdl-small-t makes P's predecessor fire launch_dependents first. P then starts early, and its profiled duration includes the wait. P rows measured after that lands are not comparable with rows measured before it. That is the main reason to run this now on the current master rather than wait. The wide variant's pre-wait prefetch is 3 x 16 KB per CTA x 216 CTAs, the same 10.4 MB as today, so it composes with the boundary PDL. (3) dense-chain-stage2 renames the module (v2) and adds Q/O kernels cloned from P. Whichever lands later needs a textual 3-way restack, not a re-measure. Do not wait on any of them. The three are mutually conflicting textually but independent in what they measure.
rules_flags: None blocking. The per-NF fallback is decided in prepare() from occupancy (a hardware property) and a synthetic self-check. Nothing is derived from the timed inputs, there is no host sync in kernel_fn, and the precision is unchanged (bf16 operands, fp32 accumulate, fixed-order split-K reduce, so the result is deterministic).

Hygiene: ws must be resized for SPLIT 6 and the ticket compare must use the wide SPLIT, not DL_SPLIT_K=3. cnt[ntile] must still be reset by the last-ticket CTA, or graph replay double-counts. The existing graph-replay self-check should run on the wide variant.
open_questions: Give the wide kernel a distinct symbol (e.g. dl_pooler_router_wide_kernel<NF>) so the profile row is unambiguous against master's dl_pooler_router_kernel<2>/<4>.

Print prepare P timing for both the old and the wide kernel at T=9/16/32 in the same run. Prepare timings undercount the profile by 20-25% (LESSONS 2026-10-25), so rank on them and judge on the profile.
Does 4 x 64-K stages keep enough K-depth in flight? If the wide variant is flat, the next probe is 3 stages of 128-K at 128 rows (W 32 KB per stage, 1-2 CTAs/SM), not a re-run.
